newsitem.title: INDIA: Protesting Kashmir separatist leaders detained.
newsitem.headline: Protesting Kashmir separatist leaders detained.

text.p: Kashmir separatist leaders were detained by police on Thursday when they went on hunger strike against the alleged killings in custody of four guerrillas, witnesses said.

A police spokesman said three leaders and half a dozen supporters of Kashmir's All Party Hurriyat (Freedom) Conference, the main separatist group, and Javed Mir of the Jammu and Kashmir Liberation Front were taken into custody while they were protesting at Abiguzar in Srinagar, the state's summer capital.
Four militant leaders of the pro-Pakistan Hizb-ul Mujahideen were arrested at Abiguzar recently.
Police said the guerrillas were killed in two shootouts with paramilitary troops last week. The Hurriyat leaders said they were killed by their captors.
The Hurriyat leaders carried placards saying "Stop custodial killings" and "Shame India".
Guerrillas are fighting for the merger of Jammu and Kashmir state with neighbouring Pakistan, which has fought two wars with India over the region since independence from Britain in 1947.
More than a dozen militant groups are fighting New Delhi's rule in the Himalayan state, where police and hospitals say more than 20,000 people have been killed in a seven-year-old rebellion.
